headline: Funding flows. Space traffic resumes. Satellites multiply.
deck: This week sees renewed investments and legislative shifts in the space sector.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in its Series C funding round, underscoring the growing demand for co-orbital security solutions. The company is positioning itself as a key player in space domain awareness, benefiting from a notable pull-through from the Department of Defense. With this funding, True Anomaly aims to enhance its capabilities in a market where competition is heating up.
stories.soWhat: Investors are clearly betting that space security will be a priority, even if the tech behind it still feels like a work in progress.

stories.head: House restores funding for TraCSS amid traffic concerns
stories.body: In a surprising turn, the House has restored funding for the Traffic Coordination and Surveillance System (TraCSS), a move that reflects growing concerns about space traffic management. This funding could help avert potential collisions as satellite launches are projected to exceed 7,000 annually by the mid-2030s. The decision highlights a shift in priorities as lawmakers grapple with the implications of a crowded orbital environment.
stories.soWhat: Bureaucracies can change their minds—who knew? This could mean a more structured approach to space traffic, which some might argue is long overdue.

stories.head: Anduril teams with L3Harris for tactical SDA constellation
stories.body: Anduril and L3Harris have teamed up to bid for a tactical Space Development Agency constellation, signaling a collaborative effort to enhance U.S. capabilities in space. This partnership comes at a time when the government is ramping up its focus on space resilience, as evidenced by the recent $1.4 billion increase in the FY27 budget for this purpose. Their combined expertise could provide a competitive edge in defense contracts.
stories.soWhat: In a sector where collaboration can make or break a bid, this partnership might just be the tactical advantage they need to navigate the complex defense landscape.

watchlist.title: SpaceX valuation hits $470 billion
watchlist.body: With SpaceX's secondary market valuation soaring, expect more discussions about its impact on the broader aerospace investment landscape.

watchlist.title: Hypersonic glide-vehicle test delays continue
watchlist.body: As the hypersonic glide-vehicle test slips for the third consecutive quarter, the implications for defense readiness are becoming increasingly concerning.

watchlist.title: Tomorrow.io's funding brings total to $210 million
watchlist.body: Tomorrow.io's recent $35 million funding round may signal a growing interest in weather satellites, potentially reshaping the market.

watchlist.title: Founders Fund reviews space portfolio
watchlist.body: The Founders Fund's quiet portfolio review could indicate strategic shifts in their investment focus, especially in the defense sector.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
